html:
SMTO-EXE-0131 — The web browser on your Gateway is too busy right now

GUID: 884413a1-ef50-5d91-8b6b-75b0e4ada437
Slug: browser-busy
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • The Gateway already has as many browser windows or browser steps going as it allows, so SMTO didn't run this step. Nothing was done on the website.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let other running tasks that use the web browser finish, or stop ones you no longer need with the Stop current task button. The Gateway runs at most 32 browser steps at once, and each running step holds a place until it ends.
  2. Ask SMTO to close any browser sessions it opened that you no longer need, then ask it to do the step again. The Gateway allows at most eight open browser sessions at a time, including ones opened by other conversations.
  3. If this keeps happening after the Gateway has been running a long time, ask the person who manages SMTO to restart the Gateway when no browser work is running. The Gateway only accepts 8,192 browser steps in total before it needs a restart to accept more.

What success looks like

  • SMTO runs the browser step and tells you what happened on the page.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Gateway's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Ask them not to restart the Gateway while a browser step is still running, because a half-finished click or form would then be hard to check.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Browser admission refused the call because the Gateway already has 8 open or starting sessions, 32 active operations, or 8,192 finished execution IDs recorded since the browser service started.

What this means

  • Admission reached eight current/pending sessions, thirty-two active operations or the service-lifetime fence of 8,192 finished execution IDs. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Admission reached eight current/pending sessions, thirty-two active operations or the service-lifetime fence of 8,192 finished execution IDs.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify which bound was reached; stopping a session does not remove the lifetime execution-identity fence.

How to fix it

  • List and stop unused sessions (browser.sessions, browser.stop) or wait for active operations to finish. If the 8,192-entry finished-ID set in BrowserService (src/gateway_core/browser/service.py) is full, restart the Gateway, but only after confirming in-flight mutations have settled with browser.page_info or browser.snapshot, because IDs are never released during a service lifetime.
  • Wait for active operations, stop unused sessions, or restart the Gateway after reconciling all uncertain effects if the identity fence is full.

Retry and execution caution

  • Wait for active operations, stop unused sessions, or restart the Gateway after reconciling all uncertain effects if the identity fence is full.

How to verify the fix

  • Capacity is released by owned-work lifecycle controls, or a deliberately managed restart occurs only after original effects are reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
